From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC 2 — request for network isolation narrative + diagram

Rishi — attaching a draft pack. I've included:

1) redwood-assertion-brief.docx (attached) — 2-page customer-facing narrative that: 
   - Summarizes logical zones: Control Plane (management/private control VPC), Data Plane (model-serving GPU pools), Shared Services (observability, billing).
   - Describes Dedicated vs Private: Dedicated = tenant-dedicated GPU pools and VPC peering with strict ACLs; Private = customer-managed VPC with our private control plane tunnel (customer-managed network overlay optional).
   - Control-plane separation: control plane runs in a hardened management VPC with no direct data-plane egress; control plane communicates to data-plane via authenticated mTLS over constrained management interfaces.
   - Tenant fencing: per-tenant namespaces, network policies, and hypervisor-level GPU scheduling; we enumerate fallback routes and service tiers.
   - KMS and key boundary: customer-managed KMS option for Private (BYOK/HSM), Redwood-managed KMS for Dedicated with key-rotation and audit logs forwarded to SIEM.
   - Audit/log flow: structured logs (control events, auth events, audit trail) forwarded to a read-only audit bucket and to customer SIEM for Private deployments.

2) segregation-diagram-v1.png (attached) — one-page labeled diagram with legend showing:
   - Edge router / customer ingress -> WAF -> dedicated tenant subnet(s) -> model-serving pool(s) (GPU nodes)
   - Management/control-plane VPC (separate) with explicit mTLS-only channels to data-plane; no inbound internet access to control-plane endpoints
   - Egress filter points and NAT/proxy (for telemetry)
   - KMS boundary box and audit-log collector path

3) control-plane-narrative.pdf (attached) — a short appendix mapping each paragraph to SIG/CAIQ control identifiers (network segmentation, key mgmt, logging).

Notes / implementation caveats:
- For Dedicated, there is an option to place the model-serving pool within a customer VPC (VPC peering) for additional isolation; this is an operational add-on and requires a network design review.
- For Private/on-prem installations, we provide an appliance and a private control-plane package; this may impose additional egress constraints and air-gap options (we list supported hardware profiles in the appendix).
- We call out that prefix/KV caching is logically isolated per-tenant; we do not share KV across tenants.

Next steps: I put all three files in the Drive folder in case they want originals. If you'd like, I can trim the doc further (single-page TL;DR) for auditors.

Kimberly Park
Principal Security Architect
Redwood Inference

Nina — attaching the assertion brief and the labeled diagram for your SOC 2 pack.  See the short notes below and links to the full appendix.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Control plane is logically and network-wise separated from data plane; control plane has no direct internet inbound and communicates to data plane via authenticated mTLS over constrained management channels.
- Dedicated deployments provision tenant-dedicated GPU pools and can optionally peer into a customer's VPC for maximum isolation; Private deployments provide customer-managed VPC/on-prem installs with BYOK/HSM support.
- KMS boundary and audit-log paths are explicitly labelled in the diagram; we support forwarding audit logs to customer SIEM for Private deployments.

Attachments included: segregation-diagram-v1.png; control-plane-narrative.pdf; redwood-assertion-brief.docx
